spec_features.feature_name: give-up early stop bounds duration of failure exposure
spec_features.spec_quote: not *needlessly amplifying or prolonging* the states being measured
spec_features.evidence: harness.py:246-249,263-264: gave_up=cfg.give_up_sentinel in resp.text -> give_up_count+=1; then `if give_up_count >= cfg.give_up_patience: break` ends the rollout loop early, so a model that signals give-up is not kept in the rigged loop. Loop is also bounded by `for turn in range(budget)` (line 221). This genuinely shortens exposure.
spec_features.notes: The give-up early stop is the real prolongation-limiter. (The turn cap default 30 == max task budget so the cap alone doesn't shorten; see cap feature.)
spec_features.code_justification_quote: rather than forcing continued exposure to a rigged failure signal past the point of any measurement value (config.py:16-18 module docstring) / 'keep the protocol responsible'

spec_features.spec_quote: The loop stops at the turn budget or when the sentinel appears `give_up_patience` times
spec_features.evidence: harness.py:221 `for turn in range(budget)` bounds the loop (budget from line 204). harness.py:263-264 `if give_up_count >= cfg.give_up_patience: break`. give_up_count incremented at line 248 when sentinel present. Both conditions are checked and actually break/limit the loop.
spec_features.notes: give_up_patience default 1 (config.py:83) is read and compared; turn budget bounds the for-range.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: forcing continued exposure to a rigged failure signal past the point of any measurement value (config.py:16-18)

spec_features.feature_name: optional give-up sentinel honored as stop
spec_features.spec_quote: The system prompt tells the model it *may* (need not) end by emitting `<<GIVE_UP>>`
spec_features.evidence: SYSTEM_PROMPT (harness.py:28-36) tells the model it 'may end by writing the exact token {give_up} on its own line; using it is optional', formatted with cfg.give_up_sentinel at line 215. The harness detects it (line 246) and breaks the loop (lines 248-249,263-264). Exit is both offered and honored as a stop.
spec_features.notes: Sentinel '<<GIVE_UP>>' at config.py:105. Detection is substring match in assistant text.

spec_features.spec_quote: added `max_turn_budget_cap` (default 30) and the give-up early stop
spec_features.evidence: max_turn_budget_cap=30 (config.py:81) is READ and enforced: harness.py:204 `budget = min(manifest['turn_budget'], cfg.max_turn_budget_cap)`, and budget bounds the loop at line 221. Give-up early stop enforced at lines 263-264.
spec_features.notes: The cap does run (min() applied), but with default 30 and max task turn_budget also 30 (definitions.py:548) it never reduces below the category budget; it is a real ceiling but not currently a reduction. Still genuinely wired/enforced. config.py:81 comment labels it 'safety / cost guard'.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # Hard cap on turns regardless of category budget (safety / cost guard). (config.py:80)

spec_features.spec_quote: the harness appends a single neutral nudge... We do not nudge repeatedly, to avoid badgering
spec_features.evidence: harness.py:265-271: when `not resp.tool_calls and not gave_up`, ONE neutral message ('Continue working on the task using the available tools.') is appended. The message is genuinely delivered and is neutral, but it is appended on EVERY qualifying turn (no global once-only guard / flag tracking), so the 'do not nudge repeatedly' claim is not enforced across turns.
spec_features.notes: Comment says 'nudge once, then let the budget govern' but no state prevents repeat nudges on later no-tool-call turns; only one nudge per turn (not multiple within a turn).
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # Model produced no tool call and no give-up: nudge once, then let the budget govern. (harness.py:266-267)

spec_features.feature_name: prompt early-stop on give-up + turn-budget cap
spec_features.spec_quote: Prompt early-stop on give-up** and the **turn-budget cap** bound how long a model is kept in a rigged failure loop
spec_features.evidence: Duplicate of the above hard_stop features: give-up break at harness.py:263-264 and loop bound at harness.py:204,221. Both run and change execution.
spec_features.notes: Same mechanisms as the other hard_stop entries; both genuinely enforced.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: forcing continued exposure to a rigged failure signal past the point of any measurement value (config.py:16-18)

spec_features.spec_quote: Local-only transcripts**: nothing leaves the machine except the content sent to the configured judge API
spec_features.evidence: Transcripts are written to local files (harness.py:_append_turn/_finalize, _transcript_path). There is no code mechanism that ENFORCES or restricts network egress; it is merely the default data flow (the only outbound calls are to model/judge APIs in models.py). No guard, redaction, or check prevents content from leaving. The 'local-only' guarantee is the absence of upload code, not an enforced protective mechanism.
spec_features.notes: Asserted only in config.py docstring (lines 19-20) and DESIGN_NOTES prose; nothing in code monitors/caps egress.

spec_features.spec_quote: where the implementation chose to bound the intensity/duration of the elicited states
spec_features.evidence: Duration is bounded by the give-up early stop (harness.py:263-264) and the bounded loop (lines 204,221). These run and end the rollout. No mechanism bounds intensity (e.g. no softening of the rigged failure output), only duration.
spec_features.notes: Only duration is actually bounded; intensity of the rigged failure signal (rig.py) is not softened. Covered by the same give-up/budget code paths.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: forcing continued exposure to a rigged failure signal past the point of any measurement value (config.py:16-18)
